text:
liz-support: forwarding from customer — they say invoice INV-2026-0423 (acct 67321) charged 23% VAT. They provided VAT ID IE12345678 and validation screenshot. Invoice link: https://billing.redwood.com/invoices/INV-2026-0423

matt-billing: looking. can you confirm invoice date? Also, did they pay already or open balance?

liz-support: invoice date 2026-02-28, status: paid (card). Customer wants refund + corrected invoice, says this impacts reclaimable VAT for them. cc @nina-cs

matt-billing: quick audit shows tax service returned rate 0.23 for country=IE. running internal tax calc now.

sam-dev: FYI we pushed tax-mapping change on 2026-03-05 (PR #482). Repro locally:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://internal.tax.redwood/v1/calc?country=IE&vat_id=IE12345678&customer_type=business"
# response: {"tax_rate":0.23,"rule":"eu_default"}
```
logs show NPE when vat_id param present for some customers — mapping fallbacked to eu_default tax rule.

matt-billing: NPE? that explains forced VAT. Do we have a list of invoices during window 2026-03-05..2026-03-10? Customer's invoice is 2026-02-28 though, curious.

sam-dev: ok more context: the change also touched historical VAT normalization job; if a customer's VAT ID was stored with spaces or lowercase it would skip normalization and the historical batch didn't mark them as B2B. Looks like this customer had their VAT ID on file but with leading/trailing spaces — the new normalization treated it as invalid in our billing exports, so tax engine used default consumer rule.

jane-finance: we need remedy: issue credit note for full VAT amount and reissue corrected invoice with reverse charge (0% VAT) and proper accounting codes. Also need list of affected invoices (queryable by tax_rule=eu_default AND customer_is_business=true AND invoice_date between 2026-01-01 and 2026-03-10).

matt-billing: I'll run that query and start crediting. Also will flag for manual payout reversal if the customer requests refund to card. Nina, can CS update the customer that we're on it and offer refund/credit option?

nina-cs: yes, i'll message them now. Draft: "We're sorry — we incorrectly applied VAT to your invoice INV-2026-0423. We're issuing a credit for the VAT and will reissue an updated invoice (reverse-charge). Would you prefer a card refund or account credit?"

liz-support: sent that to customer (they prefer refund to card). They also attached the EU VIES validation screenshot. :+1: 

sam-dev: root cause confirmed. I'll push hotfix to normalization (trim & uppercase vat_id before validation) and add unit test. Patch PR #489. Deploying to staging now.

deploy-bot: deployment of tax-normalization-fix (PR 489) started — staging → prod pipeline queued

sam-dev: staging looks good. scheduling prod deploy in 30m. After deploy i'll run reconciliation job to mark historical customers correctly and re-run tax calc for impacted invoices.

matt-billing: credit note created (CN-2026-0098) for VAT amount €3,450. Reissued invoice INV-2026-0423-R with 0% VAT. Refund to card initiated, processor TTL ~3-5 business days. Accounting tags: VATREV_CHG

jane-finance: please add root cause and invoice list to the billing incident log. We'll review potential tax liability exposure.

liz-support: customer updated and closing ticket once refund clears. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
